https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-.text: BERLIN — Germany’s increasingly embattled Chancellor Friedrich Merz conceded that a key regional election on Sunday was a “disaster” as exit polls suggested the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party was on course for its second win in two weeks. He pushed back, however, against increasing speculation that he would have to step down and vowed to push through his reform agenda as chancellor with “backbone, steadfastness, and patience.” An exit poll on the ARD broadcaster put the AfD’s vote in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania at 37% — just ahead of the center-left Social Democratic Party on 35.5%. The AfD’s national co-leader, Tino Chrupalla, called the initial Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania result a “sensation.” Advertisement Advertisement That result comes hard on the heels of the vote in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sept. 6 where the far right won so convincingly that it could potentially now govern a German state for the first time since the 1940s. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the SPD should have sufficient support to form a coalition and stop the AfD running the state, but the results for Merz’s Christian Democratic Union were catastrophic. It won only 5.5% of the vote, according to the exit poll — the worst outcome for his party in any regional or national election since the end of World War II. “We can’t sugarcoat the results in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. It’s a disaster. The CDU fought hard, but in the end, it was crushed in the escalating confrontation between the SPD and the AfD,” Merz said after the exit polls. While the CDU’s unpopularity has sparked discussion of a Kanzlertausch — or chancellor swap — Merz responded to his party’s regional drubbing by doubling down on his pledge to deliver on a reform agenda. “Germany is capable of reform. I would even go so far as to say that these reforms are the antidote to the poison of authoritarianism,” he said. “What needs to be done now requires backbone, steadfastness, and patience. I will demonstrate these qualities as chairman of the CDU and, above all, as chancellor of our country.” Merz has staked his chancellorship on tackling economic and welfare reforms that previous governments deemed too politically difficult, even branding himself the “reform chancellor.” His agenda includes raising the retirement age to shore up the pension system, cutting some health-insurance benefits to curb rising premiums and making it harder for workers to take sick leave in an effort to boost growth. In Berlin, Die Linke, or the Left party, is on course to finish first with 24.5%, according to the ARD exit poll, ahead of Merz’s CDU on 20%, which currently controls the mayor’s office in the capital. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Donald Trump on stage with Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, in Washington DC on 29 September 2026. Photograph: Alex Brandon/AP View image in fullscreen Donald Trump on stage with Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, in Washington DC on 29 September 2026. Photograph: Alex Brandon/AP Trump administration Trump names intelligence chief Jay Clayton as new White House AI czar Calyton said AI was a ‘gamechanger’ but it also posed ‘a threat’ during his DNI Senate confirmation hearing Ariana Baio Sun 4 Oct 2026 09.44 EDT Last modified on Sun 4 Oct 2026 09.47 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump on Sunday named Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence , to serve also as the new White House AI czar. Clayton, who leads the US’s 18 intelligence agencies , previously served as the top federal prosecutor in Manhattan and led the Securities and Exchange Commission during Trump’s first term. During his Senate confirmation hearing , Clayton said AI was a “gamechanger”, but it also posed “a threat”. “When something’s both an opportunity and a threat, you better get your arms around it,” Clayton told lawmakers when asked about AI. CBS News was the first to report that Clayton would be appointed White House AI czar. In a social media post on Sunday, Trump announced that Clayton would lead what the US president called “the Super Intelligence Force (SIF)”. Trump’s post also said the SIF would “coordinate the federal government’s engagement with consumers, public interest groups, religious organizations, critical infrastructure providers, and super intelligence companies”. In September, Trump announced he was creating an “AI Force” and a czar to oversee the technology’s growth and monitor for “bad” development. The announcement came after tech industry leaders warned that AI was developing too rapidly to control and that it could harm humans. The president has largely brushed aside concerns about AI development and the construction of datacenters, which power the technology. Trump has insisted continued development is paramount to defeating China in the global AI race. But to address concerns, the president created an advisory committee in addition to the czar – who he previously promised would be led by a “High IQ” individual. Trump also recently met with AI industry leaders to discuss concerns. On Tuesday, Trump and six executives signed an AI accord at the White House, promising to create internal and external monitors to ensure the technology is used as intended and any safety issues are addressed. Trump had initially created the AI and cryptocurrency czar position when he returned to the White House in January 2025. David Sacks, the venture capitalist and tech businessman, served as the administration’s AI and cryptocurrency czar until March 2026, when he reached his employment limit under his designation as a “special government employee”. Sacks still co-chairs the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. Trump previously floated Clayton’s name as a potential AI czar, telling Axios in September that Clayton is ‘“a good man” and the prospect of appointing him was “a good idea”. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/10/17/magy.text: Menü Kereső Magyar Péter Trump és Putyin egyezségéről: Legalább még egy évig mentesülhetünk az orosz kőolajra vonatkozó szankciók alól Belföld frissítve Madzin Emília Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Az amerikai elnök olyan megállapodást köt, amilyet akar, de azt gondolja, ha Trump megállapodást köt a dízelexportról, nem lenne logikus nem megadni Magyarországnak még legalább egy évre az orosz kőolajra vonatkozó szankciók alóli mentességet, mondta Magyar Péter az orosz-amerikai dízelmegállapodásról a 444-nek adott interjújában. „Nyilván Ukrajna szempontjából viszont nem üdvözletes a megállapodás” – tette hozzá. Az interjú még azelőtt készült, hogy Donald Trump bejelentette, nemzeti érdekre hivatkozva Trump felfüggesztette az Oroszországot célzó új szankciós csomagot, aminek eredetileg az lett volna a célja, hogy fokozza a nyomást Oroszországra a 2022-ben megkezdett ukrajnai inváziója miatt. Ennek előzményeként Trump és Vlagyimir Putyin orosz elnök dízelmegállapodást kötöttek, amivel lényegében felrúgta az orosz energiahordozók exportjára vonatkozó amerikai szankciókat. A miniszterelnök az EU-csúcsról hazafelé tartva nyilatkozott a 444-nek, többek között elismételte, hogy nem gondolja, Volodimir Zelenszkij eljönne az október 23-ai állami ünnepségre. Érintette azt is, hogy a Magyarországra kiszabott migrációs büntetés felfüggesztéséről remélhetőleg idén már sikerül megállapodniuk, már a tárgyalások véghajrájában vannak. „Annyi értelme volt, hogy beszéltem az Európai Bizottság elnökével, és azért állt a tárgyalás fél óráig, mert fél mondatot bele kellett rakatnom a tanácsi következtetésekbe az illegális migráció instrumentalizációjával kapcsolatban.” Arról, hogy visszakap-e valamennyit Magyarország az eddig befizetett büntetésből kompenzációként, azt mondta, „nyilván a plénum előtt nem tesznek erre ígéretet, de mivel ez egy egyhangú dosszié, és nagyon meg szeretnének állapodni decemberben, azt gondolom, jó eséllyel indulunk.” A magyar kormányfő második EU-csúcstalálkozója az elmúlt évek leghosszabbja lett: a 2024 óta tartó szokásoktól eltérően egy nap helyett eleve kettővel számoltak, és már a csütörtöki rész is elhúzódott . Magyar szerint „volt itt minden: vétófenyegetés, kiabálás, szövetségek és óriási viták”, de „minden fontos kérdésben győzött a magyar érdek”. A mostani EU-csúcsról részletesen ebben a cikkben írtunk.
